note: One file, two consumers: the Gallery renders its parity strip from it, and tests/FluentJalium.Tests/Gallery/AstraGalleryCatalogTests.cs fails when it stops matching the styles Astra actually ships. Scope is the implicit-style universe - every TargetType a product dictionary restyles without an x:Key - because that is the set an app inherits silently.

parityLegend.audited: Upstream dictionary transcribed key for key with its blob recorded, states mapped, and at least one pixel assertion. Whatever is missing is named in gaps.
parityLegend.ported: Style came from the pre-Astra adapter and consumes Astra tokens, but the upstream key list was never transcribed verbatim and no pixel assertion covers it.
parityLegend.own-type: Jalium has no native type for this control, so an Astra-owned type carries the behavior; adaptation/05 records the demonstrated gap.
parityLegend.no-upstream-control: The pinned WinUI commit carries no such control at all (the search is recorded in the cited audit), so the look is built on the token row that commit does ship plus the divider-role templates around it. Nothing on this row is claimed as a key-for-key transcription.

the framework gives this type no template and draws its own line in code from its own row, but does build ours, so two paths can paint the same pixel: our row is the one the capture reads, and a host build that draws without the template would show the framework's grey
no state cells: a separator has no hover, press or checked state here, and upstream gives it none either
the half-DIP corner radius on the line is a literal - upstream publishes it as an x:Double row this reader cannot parse
the rule has no height of its own, as upstream: the 2,8,2,8 is the rectangle's margin and the bar's row is what sizes it

surface and geometry only: the control stores a Template and never builds one, so its code-built StackPanel, its 40x32 ellipsis button and its overflow Popup stay host-drawn and follow just the three rows its code reads

the open state never displays: setting IsOpen moves that property only - the bar's own Popup stays closed in-process - so CommandBarBackgroundOpen, the ellipsis icon rows, the light-dismiss overlay and the overflow-presenter borders are withheld, and AstraAppBarTests.The_open_bar_shows_its_overflow_outside_the_surface_this_capture_can_reach pins why no row of that state can be promised to an app
a SplitButton placed in the bar keeps its non-app-bar style: upstream's SplitButtonInAppBarUnfocusedPointerOver and a CommandBar-scoped SplitButton style are still owed by this family

the bar's 48-tall closed height is a literal on the style; upstream's AppBarThemeMinHeight / AppBarThemeCompactHeight pair are x:Double rows this reader cannot parse, and no compact height is set at all

Own type, not the runtime's TabControl: a TabControl handed a template - through a style setter or a local value - builds no tree at all, its realized tree is unchanged, and its strip's measure collapses to 0 wide (spike/TabViewStyle sections D-G, adaptation/00 S1-h). A ContentControl subclass on the same route does build (section I), which is what this type and its item are.

No drag, no drop and no reorder: upstream's CanDragTabs, CanReorderTabs and AllowDropTabs with their eleven drag and reorder VisualStates, the TabItemDragStarting/TabItemDropDetected/TabItemsReorderEnded events and the TabDragVisualContainer part are absent here.

No overflow scroll buttons: the strip scrolls, but the two RepeatButtons upstream hangs on TabScrollViewerStyle (TabView.xaml:133-172) and their twelve TabViewScrollButton* rows are withheld rather than published unread.
No TabWidthMode: upstream's Equal/SizeToContent/Compact group and its per-tab width arithmetic are not implemented, so a strip wider than the window scrolls instead of shrinking its tabs.

The selected tab's fill is a Border rather than upstream's code-built Path: the two 4 DIP corner hooks are drawn as separate arc Paths and the fill stays square where upstream's geometry curves out (TabViewItem.cpp:98-122).

The host's SingleBottomBorderLine and NoBottomBorderLine states are not switched: both line pieces are always drawn, which is upstream's default state, and the code that decides between them is not reproduced.
No TabStripHeaderTemplate/TabStripFooterTemplate and no TabItemTemplate or selector: the two strip slots take an element, not a data template.
The Ctrl+Tab, Ctrl+Shift+Tab and Delete accelerators are handled inside the control with no KeyboardAcceleratorTextVisible surface, so no key breadcrumb is drawn anywhere.
The item's template holds no presenter for Content - the view's body presenter owns it - so the strip shows Header and the page shows Content, one parent each.

Upstream builds the selected tab's outline in code from TabViewItemTemplateSettings.TabGeometry; TopCornerRadius here is the item's own read-only row over the same value the TopCornerRadiusFilterConverter produces.
No ToolTipTitle/ToolTipText rows and no TabViewTemplateSettings surface; a long header trims to an ellipsis at the 240 DIP maximum.

No automation peer of its own: the tab is a HeaderedContentControl, so an inspector sees a text control rather than a SelectionItem, and this runtime cannot synthesize a KeyEventArgs to prove the keyboard path end to end (spike/TabViewProbe section C).

the indeterminate bar is a still picture: spike/ProgressProbe mode F measured that a repeating animation on TranslateTransform.XProperty and on RotateTransform.AngleProperty never advances on 26.10.9 while Width and Canvas.Left do, and a Storyboard read out of markup hydrates with zero children - so upstream's two-bar slide has no declarative route and no animator is wired for it
ShowError and ShowPaused do not exist on the host's ProgressBar, so upstream's Error and Paused states - and the two foreground rows they read - are not published at all

there is no ProgressBarTemplateSettings here, so TemplateSettings.ClipRect and IndicatorLengthDelta (ProgressBar.cpp:195, :246) are dropped rather than faked: no clip layer, no reposition rebound on the Updating-to-Determinate transition
the 3 DIP band and the 1 DIP rail are literals in the template: ProgressBarMinHeight and ProgressBarTrackHeight are x:Double rows this markup reader rejects outright, not silently drops
upstream declares no Orientation at all, so the vertical band this layer honours is a host extra, asserted as geometry and not as parity
no pointer or touch evidence: the bar takes no input, so nothing on this page is claimed as an interaction path

own type, because the runtime exports neither ProgressRing nor the AnimatedVisualPlayer its template hosts - and no Lottie reader either, so the two shipped assets are not carried and the look is rebuilt from the numbers inside them

the indeterminate arc keeps its half circle while it turns: upstream's asset also animates TrimStart from 0 to 0.5 across the loop (ProgressRingIndeterminate.cpp:305, :318), which is the taper at the trailing end, and nothing here reproduces it

the rotation is written into the figure rather than onto a RenderTransform, because the transform route was never measured clean: the first cut's empty-looking picture turned out to be an integer-division constant, so the pivot question stays open

DeterminateSource and IndeterminateSource (IAnimatedVisualSource, MUX_PREVIEW) have no counterpart, and ProgressRingTemplateSettings is absent, so ApplyTemplateSettings' EllipseDiameter/EllipseOffset/MaxSideLength arithmetic is carried as constants in the control instead of as a bindable surface
ProgressRingStrokeThickness is not published: this reader rejects an x:Double row outright and upstream's own template never reads it
the Inactive state's AccessibilityView=Raw has no member here, so an inactive ring leaves the accessibility tree by opacity only
the 359.9 degree cap and the -90 start follow ModernWpf's reading rather than the asset, which no tool in this repository can inspect
high contrast resolves through the palette aliases instead of upstream's two re-pointed rows
no pointer or touch evidence: upstream sets IsHitTestVisible=False and IsTabStop=False, both asserted, so the ring has no interaction arm to prove
the reference commit has no Divider control - zero files by name and no Divider type in any .idl or .h - so this row cannot claim a transcription, a state map or a key list against upstream

the 1 DIP thickness is the only number every divider-role template in the commit agrees on; the 12 DIP box the line sits in is the runtime's own measurement of Separator and is asserted as measured, not as parity
no margin is set: upstream's role-specific margins (2,8,2,8 on the app-bar pair, 0,3,0,4 in the sidebar, 0,8,0,8 between tabs) belong to their hosts and none of them is a general divider's

the line is the control's own OnRender output, not a template: a templated route was measured and works, but the element upstream reaches for - a 1 DIP Rectangle - prints nothing on this runtime, and the five such rectangles already shipped in the table and app-bar styles are an open defect
no key is published here: the file consumes the palette's DividerStrokeColorDefaultBrush, whose high-contrast re-point is that layer's job
the framework's own default line colour before this style existed is a grey (#A3A3A4) this layer reproduces nowhere, so the before/after reading is a probe record rather than a parity claim
no pointer or touch evidence: the runtime already keeps the separator out of the hit-test path, so there is no interaction arm to prove
own type, because the runtime exports neither InfoBadge nor Badge; the sixteen style keys, the two aliases, the four Thickness rows and every number in the look are upstream's

the icon input is an IconElement, not upstream's IconSource: IconSource, FontIconSource, SymbolIconSource, PathIconSource, BitmapIconSource and ImageIconSource are all absent, so there is no object that property could hold

a style's Setter.Value holds one element instance, so the five icon styles each carry a single FontIcon/SymbolIcon shared by every badge of that style - tree-level independence is measured, visual independence is not

six x:Double rows are not published: this reader rejects an x:Double element outright and carries a clr-namespace numeric row as the type's default, so the four the template reads are literals and the two nobody upstream reads are not written at all

InfoBadgeIconHeight differs per theme upstream (8 in the dark dictionary, 9 in the light two) and no numeric row can carry a theme-dependent number here - immaterial, because nothing in upstream consumes the row

the number's ink cannot be asserted: neither capture path reaches a glyph run (adaptation/00 S1-r clause 3), so the value state is proven by Text, Visibility, the foreground brush identity and the measured box rather than by pixels
the template's TextBlock needs an explicit Foreground binding: parts do not inherit the control's foreground here, and upstream's row relies on inheritance
no Severity enum and no AutomationPeer upstream either - the five severities are style keys only - and high contrast re-points underneath the aliases in the palette layer rather than in this file
no pointer or touch evidence: upstream declares no events and its style sets IsTabStop=False, so there is no interaction arm to prove
